newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won barely changed, traders sidelined.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won barely changed, traders sidelined.

text.p: The won was little changed on Wednesday with most market players sitting on the sidelines, dealers said.
They said traders differed in their views over the future direction on fears of central bank's dollar buying intervention and long dollar positions.
The won finished at 890.90, comparing with Tuesday's close of 891.00. It hit a low of 891.20 on dollar buying interest at low level.
"The dollar is unlikely to rise further from a mid-term point of view," said a dealer.
"If the dollar jumps to the 892 won level, the number of sellers will shrink," said another dealer. "The upward trend to the 893.30 shown last month still lives in the market."
Trading volume was estimated at $1.12 billion.
Dealers forecast Thursday's mid-rate would be pegged at 891.00, unchanged from today.
